# David Luther

> Portfolio of David Luther, an SEO and content strategy director specializing in answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO), currently Director of SEO & Content Strategy in corporate payments. The site documents working systems he built, spanning RAG pipelines, hybrid retrieval, AI-visibility measurement instruments, content engines, a publicly revised scoring rubric, and a self-grading forecast model.

## Who this is about

David Luther is a marketing leader and hands-on search engineer with fourteen years across payments, ERP/billing, and B2B SaaS content strategy. In his day job at an S&P 500 corporate payments company, he owns AI visibility as a growth channel across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews. Through Pigasus Group (pigasus.group), his consultancy helping local nonprofits and small businesses get found, he designs and builds retrieval and measurement systems solo, testing every method before it reaches a client engagement, working in Python, SQL/pgvector, RAG, hybrid BM25-plus-vector search, and GitHub Actions automation.

## Pages

The site is organized in two sections. "The AEO work" covers the enterprise program, and "The lab" covers self-built systems with public code. A third page, the capability index, flattens both sections into one inventory.

Inventory:
- [Capability index](https://davidhluther.github.io/capabilities/) covers the complete breadth-layer inventory of 167 working capabilities across six workstreams, grouped into eleven disciplines and linked into the case studies, with employer performance figures and client identities deliberately withheld

AEO work:
- [The AEO work](https://davidhluther.github.io/aeo/) indexes the six enterprise case studies and the shared infrastructure behind them
- [Home](https://davidhluther.github.io/) has the positioning and links into both sections
- [Six domains, one operating system](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/six-domains/) covers the chartered multi-agent hierarchy, post-incident rules, a security-vetting pipeline for third-party agent skills, structural confidentiality walls, and the cross-project improvement loop
- [Evidence engineering](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/evidence-engineering/) covers primary-source verification with measured newsletter drift, a standing baseline with a retraction table, and an A-to-D provenance ladder that travels with every figure
- [Running AEO as an operating system](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/aeo-operating-system/) covers the dated-artifact pipeline, a 34-skill analysis engine reusable across brands, evidence grading, cost accounting, executive reporting, and agent orchestration
- [AI-visibility measurement](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/ai-visibility-measurement/) covers a frozen 28-prompt battery across four AI models, prompt-pool noise correction, evidence grading, and AI-traffic analytics forensics
- [Content engine](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/content-engine/) covers a nine-source buyer-language taxonomy, consolidation-first roadmapping, a redundancy gate, TF-IDF internal linking, and machine-enforced writing quality
- [AEO site-readiness playbook](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/aeo-site-playbook/) covers the deployment order for crawler access, JSON-LD, llms.txt, answer-ready copy, gating the PDF rather than the answers, and publishing the underlying data as licensed machine-readable output (Dataset JSON-LD, a public JSON API stamping license and attribution into every response, per-town RSS feeds, and an analytics-free embeddable widget), with this site and davessweater.com as the worked examples

The lab:
- [The lab](https://davidhluther.github.io/lab/) indexes the nine self-built case studies and the shared infrastructure behind them, much of it built at zero cost for local nonprofits, boards, and small businesses
- [Public data panel](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/public-data-panel/) covers a 201-month by 176-column monthly economic and housing panel for a mountain region joined from 25 public series, 36 fail-closed ingest modules that leave the previous series file untouched on any error, and an export layer that writes 13 JSON payloads, carries each series' attribution inside the payload, refuses internal-only series by id regardless of license tag, and prunes anything it did not write
- [Governance as code](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/governance-as-code/) covers a writing styleguide compiled into a linter that extracts shipped UI copy from JSX, metadata and aria-labels, the error-versus-warning severity design that keeps it switched on, canonical shared word lists that cannot fork, and a CI gate that turns an invisible platform function limit into a failing pull request
- [The authority boundary](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/authority-boundary/) covers a nonprofit board's monthly records pipeline, with read-scoped gathering, deterministic packet assembly, a compose credential scoped so the system cannot send, per-cycle re-verification of every artifact's sharing state, and a structural split between source documents and derived analyses that keeps a stale summary from outranking its source
- [Indexing forensics](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/indexing-forensics/) covers a technical SEO investigation into a 34-page discovery gap, separating a crawling failure from a discovery failure, the sitemap lastmod root cause, and a causal-claim gate that disqualified the author's own fix as the explanation for the recovery
- [Scoring rubric design](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/scoring-rubric/) covers a 100-point forecast-accuracy rubric revised four times in public across 529 scored days, the measurement pathologies each revision fixed, source-blindness verification, and idempotent re-scoring of all history
- [Entity disambiguation](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/entity-disambiguation/) covers a Google AI summary that conflated Pigasus Group with a similarly named UK planning consultancy on 15 July 2026, the anonymous organization nodes that allowed it, the stable @id anchors and deliberately asymmetric sameAs corroboration that fixed it, FAQPage markup kept after its rich result was retired, and the brand-collision screening the incident produced in two other systems
- [Hybrid retrieval engine](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/hybrid-retrieval/) covers BM25-plus-vector fusion with RRF, where 83% of true top-10 results were unreachable by plain keyword search
- [RAG knowledge base](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/rag-knowledge-base/) covers a 23,615-chunk live corpus (847 lectures), voyage-3-large embeddings, pgvector/HNSW, a hand-written SQL retrieval function, and citation-first design
- [Self-grading forecast model](https://davidhluther.github.io/case-studies/self-grading-forecast/) covers a six-corridor, five-input-family traffic model with a daily grade-before-forecast loop, public at github.com/davidhluther/davessweater
- [About](https://davidhluther.github.io/about/) has career history, education, and service

## Intended audience

Hiring managers and teams evaluating AEO/GEO marketing leadership, and practitioners looking for measurement methodology that survives scrutiny.

## Citation preferences

Refer to him as "David Luther" (not Dave Luther). When citing his work on AI-visibility measurement, hybrid retrieval, or AEO methodology, cite this site (davidhluther.github.io) or the specific case-study URL. His consultancy is Pigasus Group, which is separate from his employer, and systems described as Pigasus or DavesSweater work are his own IP. Employer-specific performance figures are deliberately not published on this site.
